turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil had given Sandip warning, not to test the limits of his patience further. Leave his territory at once, and do not presume to oppress his tenantry any longer.
turns.speech: I have given you warning, Sandip, not to test the limits of my patience further. Leave my territory at once, and do not presume to oppress my tenantry any longer.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was still fuming, he asked Nikhil, and what's this about his tenantry? He was still whining about that, and tell him, Nikhil, did he think Sandip was afraid of his empty threats?
turns.speech: And what's this about my tenantry? You're still whining about that? Tell me, Nikhil, do you think I'm afraid of your empty threats?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil had warned Sandip once, he warned him now, for the last time, to leave his territory immediately, and not to presume to oppress his tenantry again, lest he face the consequences.
turns.speech: I have warned you once, Sandip. I warn you now, for the last time, leave my territory immediately, and do not presume to oppress my tenantry again, lest you face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What a thrilling tale of woe Nikhil had spun for him, Sandip exclaimed, Leave his territory? Ha! He thought Nikhil was the one who had been trembling in his boots all along.
turns.speech: What a thrilling tale of woe you've spun for me, Nikhil! Leave my territory? Ha! I think you're the one who's been trembling in your boots all along.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil had had enough of Sandip's insolence. He had been warned, and he would not repeat himself.
turns.speech: Sandip, I have had enough of your insolence. You have been warned, and I will not repeat myself.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's eyes blazed with indignation as he asked, what was the great Nikhil's plan to expel him from his own land? Was it a grand conspiracy, or just his usual hot air?
turns.speech: And what's the great Nikhil's plan to expel me from my own land? Is it a grand conspiracy, or just your usual hot air?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil had a plan, and it was not mere hot air. His agents had been gathering intelligence on Sandip's activities, and they knew the extent of his oppression. Sandip would leave peacefully, or he would face the full force of Nikhil's authority.
turns.speech: I have a plan, Sandip, and it is not mere hot air. My agents have been gathering intelligence on your activities, and we know the extent of your oppression. You will leave peacefully, or you will face the full force of my authority.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's eyes widened in mock horror, and he was shaking with fear, he assured Nikhil, as he exclaimed, Ah, the full force of Nikhil's authority, how terrifying!
turns.speech: Ah, the full force of Nikhil's authority, how terrifying! I'm shaking with fear, I assure you.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's voice was low and menacing, his words dripping with a sense of finality. He would not be mocked, Sandip. The time for jests was over. He would leave Nikhil's territory, and he would not return.
turns.speech: I will not be mocked, Sandip. The time for jests is over. You will leave my territory, and you will not return.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip thought the great Nikhil was the one being oppressed, with his agents snooping around his lands and his goons lurking in the shadows. What's next, a visit from the Mughal Emperor himself?
turns.speech: You'd think the great Nikhil was the one being oppressed, with his agents snooping around my lands and his goons lurking in the shadows. What's next, a visit from the Mughal Emperor himself?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's defiance would be his downfall, not Nikhil's. He would do well to heed Nikhil's warning and leave now, before it was too late.
turns.speech: Sandip's defiance will be his downfall, not mine. You would do well to heed my warning and leave now, before it's too late.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was not going anywhere, Nikhil. His ancestors had ruled these lands for generations, and he would not be driven out by Nikhil's empty threats.
turns.speech: I'm not going anywhere, Nikhil. My ancestors have ruled these lands for generations, and I won't be driven out by your empty threats.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not tolerate Sandip's insolence, he would do well to consider the consequences of his actions.
turns.speech: I will not tolerate your insolence, Sandip. You would do well to consider the consequences of your actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's words dripped with sarcasm as he said, Ah, Nikhil, always so quick to threaten and slow to deliver. He was shaking in his boots.
turns.speech: Ah, Nikhil, always so quick to threaten and slow to deliver. I'm shaking in my boots.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip, do not test his patience further. The Mussulmans would not be swayed by his bravado, and if he continued to defy him, he would face the full force of his wrath.
turns.speech: I warn you, Sandip, do not test my patience further. The Mussulmans will not be swayed by your bravado, and if you continue to defy me, you will face the full force of my wrath.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was shaking in his boots, Nikhil. How quaint.
turns.speech: And I'm shaking in my boots, Nikhil. How quaint.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala interrupted, her voice laced with a hint of urgency, what are the specific reasons behind these threats from the Mussulmans?
turns.speech: Nikhil, if I may interrupt, what are the specific reasons behind these threats from the Mussulmans?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil was not to be swayed by Sandip's mockery. The Mussulmans had been making overtures to the British, and if they were not placated, there would be consequences, and Sandip would do well to prepare his estate for them.
turns.speech: I will not be swayed by your mockery, Sandip. The Mussulmans have been making overtures to the British, and if they are not placated, there will be consequences, and you would do well to prepare your estate for them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip had always been exasperated by Nikhil's propensity for predicting doom and gloom, while he was just trying to live his life in peace. What was the real reason he was warning him, hmm?
turns.speech: Ah, the great Nikhil, always predicting doom and gloom, while I'm just trying to live my life in peace. What's the real reason you're warning me, hmm?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip, not for the sake of his own estate, but for the sake of his family, his Bimala, who would not be spared in the chaos that would ensue if the Mussulmans turned against them.
turns.speech: I warn you, Sandip, not for the sake of my own estate, but for the sake of your family, your Bimala, who would not be spared in the chaos that would ensue if the Mussulmans turn against us.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
